<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | CONFIRMED |
| Confidence | HIGH |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Task Type | Verification policy safety and monorepo initialization |
| Complexity | STANDARD |

### What Was Claimed

A structurally valid required verification policy can point at the repository root of a monorepo even when the actual npm script exists only in a package directory. The failure is discovered after implementation rather than during setup, and `/forge:init` must not create or preserve an impossible local command.

### What We Found

The base already contains a validated `cwd` field and a static preflight adapter. Required commands are checked against the prepared frozen worktree before durable run initialization and before a repository writer is launched. The preflight can select `web/package.json` and rejects a root `npm test` when the root has no `test` script.

However, `/forge:init` unconditionally serializes `verification.commands` as `{}` after loading an existing policy. It provides no explicit, package-aware local-check selection and silently removes tracked local checks. Coverage does not exercise initializer behavior or the exact remediation for a missing package directory. The command execution path does honor the bound cwd, so the remaining work is to make initialization explicit and strengthen regression coverage around the safety boundary.

### Root Cause

Policy initialization has no safe verification-selection step. Its final policy assembly discards the source command map rather than either (a) preserving a statically validated command bound to the package that defines its script or (b) explicitly selecting CI-only verification. This makes setup behavior opaque and can hide a policy problem instead of reporting it with a concrete config path.

### Affected Files

| Path | Reason |
|---|---|
| `src/ui/commands.ts` | `/forge:init` policy assembly and user-visible verification selection |
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Static package/executable preflight and exact remediation errors |
| `src/core/policy.ts` | Validated verification command cwd contract |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Monorepo, missing package, and remediation regressions |
| `test/ui/commands.test.ts` | Initializer selection behavior |
| `README.md` | Document explicit CI-only/package-local setup behavior if needed |

### Evidence

- `VerificationCommandPolicy` includes `cwd`, normalized by `normalizeVerificationCommandCwd`.
- `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` checks only required commands and never spawns them.
- `assertPackageScript` reports `${configPath} verification.commands.<name>.argv` and tells the operator to set `cwd` or use CI-only verification.
- `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` invokes preflight before `RunJournal.initialize` and before `SubagentsRpcClient.spawnWorkOn`.
- `configureForgePolicy` currently sets `commands: {}` regardless of loaded policy content.

### History Findings

The repository guidance requires deterministic authority, fail-closed verification, and regression tests for every safety fix. Existing README guidance documents package-local `cwd`, while the initializer implementation does not yet expose an explicit corresponding choice.

### Recommendation

Keep the existing safe cwd/preflight contract, add an explicit initializer verification policy choice that either retains only statically valid package-bound local commands or writes an explicit CI-only policy, and add fixture tests for root-without-script versus `web`-with-script plus missing-directory remediation. Preserve runtime fail-closed behavior for commands that fail after implementation.

### Related Issues

- None identified.

### Decomposition Assessment

**Required**: no — the change is one bounded verification-policy initialization and regression-test concern.

### Acceptance Spec

- [ ] Validated repository-relative command cwd remains available and enforced.
- [ ] `/forge:init` never selects an npm script without a matching package script and makes CI-only verification explicit.
- [ ] Required local commands are statically preflighted before writer launch.
- [ ] Preflight errors identify the exact config path and concrete remediation.
- [ ] Monorepo and missing-package regressions are covered.
- [ ] Required checks that fail after implementation remain blocking.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective

Make ForgeDock initialization fail closed for impossible required local verification policies while preserving safe package-local commands and explicitly documenting CI-only verification.

### Allowed Paths

- `src/ui/commands.ts`
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `test/ui/commands.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `DESIGN.md`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change GitHub, lease, branch, merge, or reviewer authority.
- Do not execute repository scripts during `/forge:init` preflight.
- Do not add shell-source or arbitrary command configuration.
- Do not weaken required-check failure handling after implementation.
- Do not modify files outside the listed paths.

### Invariants

- Verification commands remain argv arrays with a validated repository-relative `cwd`.
- Only required commands are preflighted; optional commands retain existing behavior.
- Static preflight may inspect executable availability, directories, package manifests, and npm-compatible script names, but never runs a command.
- A new/template policy with no local commands remains valid as explicit GitHub-CI-only verification.
- A configured required command that fails after implementation remains blocking.

### Deliverables

- Preserve an existing tracked command map in `/forge:init` only after static required-command validation.
- Keep CI-only initialization explicit in the setup notification and documentation.
- Add actionable remediation for missing package directories/manifests and a monorepo regression fixture/test.
- Add initializer/preflight regression assertions without changing the protected workflow contract.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| `cwd` field | Reuse the existing parser and preflight directory resolver; document the field in the architecture contract. |
| Safe `/forge:init` policy | Validate the loaded command map before writing it; preserve valid package-bound commands instead of silently discarding them, and report CI-only when empty. |
| Preflight timing | Retain the existing `startIssue` preflight before run initialization and writer dispatch. |
| Actionable errors | Include the exact config path and a concrete cwd/config or CI-only remediation in static preflight failures. |
| Monorepo fixture | Cover a root without `test` and `web/package.json` with `test`, plus missing package remediation. |
| Fail closed after implementation | Leave `forge_verify` and review-gate required-check handling unchanged; regression tests cover status semantics already. |

### Out of Scope

- Automatic discovery or execution of every package's test suite.
- Reworking GitHub CI workflows or package-manager semantics beyond existing npm-compatible script inspection.
- Changing the trusted policy schema version.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### Relevant History

- The issue's observed failure occurs because a valid root-level command policy cannot express the package that owns its npm script.
- The base already added `cwd` normalization and static preflight, but initialization currently overwrites loaded local commands with `{}`.
- Repository guidance requires deterministic, testable authority and a regression test for each safety fix.

### Callers and Data Flow

- `/forge:init` loads and parses `.forge/config.json`, assembles the policy, and writes the tracked file.
- `ForgeWorkOnController.startIssue` prepares the frozen base worktree, statically preflights required commands, then initializes state and launches the writer.
- `forge_verify` resolves the bound command cwd and executes only the approved argv under the child environment.

### CI Surface

- `npm run check` is the required local verification command for this repository.
- GitHub CI remains the authoritative post-PR gate for configured target branches.
- Empty `verification.commands` is a supported CI-only policy and must not be treated as a local-check failure.

### Prior Findings

- Existing tests cover repository-relative cwd normalization, package script presence, executable lookup, and symlink escapes.
- Existing tests do not cover `/forge:init` preserving valid commands or making CI-only output explicit.
- Existing runtime tests establish that required verification failure remains represented as a failed/unknown gate.

### Hazards

- Silently dropping commands can remove intended local safety checks.
- Running package scripts during setup would execute untrusted repository code before writer dispatch.
- Reading symlinked package manifests outside the repository would violate the verification trust boundary.
- Changing command paths without preserving exact config-path diagnostics would make remediation ambiguous.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Architecture Plan

1. Update `/forge:init` policy assembly to statically validate and preserve the parsed tracked command map; emit explicit local-check or CI-only status (init-safe, error-path) (`cwd-policy`, `init-selection`).
2. Strengthen static preflight diagnostics for missing cwd/package metadata while retaining no-execution and repository-containment guarantees (`preflight-remediation`).
3. Extend adapter/UI regression coverage for root-without-script versus package-with-script, missing directories, exact config paths, and initialized command retention (`monorepo-fixture`, `init-selection`).
4. Document the command `cwd`, static preflight, and CI-only option in `DESIGN.md` (`cwd-policy`).
5. Run the required repository check and inspect the resulting diff before commit (`verification`, `fail-closed`).

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT:COMPLETE -->
